title: The flat closed-fibre criterion for complete local rings
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$, with maximal ideal $\overline{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and its induced $k$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $A$ and $B$ are complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Assume $f$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\overline B$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\overline{\mathfrak m}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Then $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.

proof.text: Choose the compatible Cohen power-series presentation using RingHom.exists_complete_local_map_cohen_presentation. Split the characteristic of the residue field into zero and prime. In the zero case, the injective residue-field map induced by f and the coefficient maps to the residue fields give characteristic zero of both coefficients; in the prime case use the Cohen-ring and first-parameter clauses.

Apply the fibre-equation removal theorem to this presentation and the flatness and smooth-fibre hypotheses. It supplies T over the same target coefficients, q:R->A, v:T->B, j:R->T with vj=fq and ker(v)=(ker(q))T, retaining the parameter extension and formal smoothness of the closed fibre.
Apply the parameter-preserving power-series lifting criterion to j and its smooth closed fibre. This gives adic formal smoothness of R->T.

Descend lifts directly through the surjections q and v. Regard each A-algebra D as an R-algebra via q. Composing a continuous g:B->D/J with v remains continuous because v maps m_T onto m_B. Apply universe-polymorphic adic formal smoothness to lift T->D/J to an R-linear l:T->D. For r in ker(q), l(j(r))=0 by R-linearity, so l kills ker(v)=(ker(q))T and descends by Mathlib RingHom.liftOfSurjective to B->D. Lift a in A to r in R to check A-linearity using vj=fq; lift b in B to x in T to check the quotient equality. This proves the original lifting property without an additional tensor-product formal-smoothness lemma.
